rewrites.after: This might be the largest thing in the entire universe.
rewrites.why: Its existence is disputed, so 'is the largest' states a contested claim as fact. 'Might be' keeps the superlative and opens a second question: why only might?

sources.claim: Other researchers doubt the structure exists

rewrites.after: The Hercules–Corona Borealis Great Wall, a wall of galaxies nearly ten billion light-years across.
rewrites.why: Its discoverers estimate 6.5–9.8 billion light-years. Hard rule 1 asks for the conservative figure, so 'nearly ten billion' instead of a flat ten.

sources.claim: Discoverers' estimate: 2,000–3,000 megaparsecs, about 6.5–9.8 billion light-years (Horváth, Hakkila & Bagoly, 2014)

rewrites.after: Light, the fastest thing there is, would need nearly ten billion years to cross it, most of the age of the cosmos.
rewrites.why: The original said light can't cross it in the age of the cosmos. That's false: the universe is 13.8 billion years old. The true version is still enormous, about 70% of all time so far.

sources.claim: Age of the universe: 13.8 billion years

rewrites.after: The largest thing in the universe, and we still aren't sure it's real.
rewrites.why: 'We don't know how it formed' assumed it exists. The real open question is whether it's real at all, and saying so echoes the hook for the loop.
